name: Integration Testing Common Pitfalls
description: This module lists the most common pitfalls encountered in integration testing work, so they can be actively avoided rather than rediscovered.
content:
This module lists the most common pitfalls encountered in integration testing work, so they can be actively avoided rather than rediscovered.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Validate integration testing outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
2. Measure before optimizing any integration testing bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
3. Re-check edge cases relevant to integration testing (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
4. Keep integration testing outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
5. State assumptions about integration testing explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
6. Keep integration testing changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
7. Surface known limitations of a chosen integration testing approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
8. Document any non-obvious integration testing decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Avoid introducing new integration testing abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Avoid mixing unrelated integration testing concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of integration testing correctness.
- Do not silently drop integration testing edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.

CLOSING NOTE
Revisit these integration testing guidelines if the task's constraints change significantly during the work.
